author: TEDx Talks
description:
One of the key ways to communicate with someone who has dementia is to enter their reality and meet them where they are. What if we used that tool and others when we speak to everyone? Cusato offers tips, tricks & a new way of communicating to connect and relate. #TEDxSarasota 

Kristen Cusato is a storyteller, communicator, and advocate who believes that sharing our stories can change lives. Kristen spent more than two decades in television news as an anchor/reporter in Connecticut, San Diego, Texas, and upstate New York. Her career took a profound turn more than 15 years ago when her mother was diagnosed with Lewy Body dementia. A new purpose and profession was born: teaching caregivers the language of dementia. 

Today, Kristen collaborates with researchers, caregivers, and people living with all forms of the disease to help them feel empowered. She has authored chapters in two Chicken Soup for the Soul caregiving books and hosts an award-winning podcast. 
Kristen is equally passio
title: How to connect to loved ones with dementia | Kristen Cusato | TEDxSarasota

author: TEDx Talks
description: Uncover your superpowers as a Water Bear Walk-on through the lens of a Division 1 Women’s Rower at Duke University. Chloe McGeehan describes her transformation from running forwards to rowing backwards, reflecting on what it takes to pivot into new spaces and propel through water. Chloe McGeehan is a Duke Division 1 Women’s Rower and Robertson Scholar. Chloe represented Duke at the 2025 ACC Rowing Championship as a 2xACC Honor Roll student-athlete and sole Class of 2026 walk-on. Off the water, Chloe works on stem cell reprogramming research in the Charlie Gersbach laboratory within the Duke Center for Advanced Genomic Technologies. She is also one of four undergraduate students working with the Duke Board of Trustees, advising the trajectory of Duke’s most ambitious campaign in history to bolster the innovation and marketability of Duke Science and Technology. Emphasizing curiosity, resilience, and trust, Chloe takes a microscopic approach in her talk to explore the capabilities withi
title: Water bear walk-on: Discovering your different path | Chloe McGeehan | TEDxDuke

author: TEDx Talks
description: We have officially entered the era of Netflix originals and classic remakes. As major production companies produces television and film for us to watch, it is time we contend with the pervasive "Single Story" of Africa, and moreso, how it is so singluar.  Comfort Markwei is a senior at Duke University double double-majoring in History and International Comparative Studies. She was raised in Nashville, Tennessee, by two Ghanaian immigrants along with her two younger siblings. Her professional interests are in law, intellectual property, and cultural production. She asks how film and television specifically act as spaces for cultural production, and how heritage and representation are protected in an industry that commodifies stories. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: We shouldn't settle for the single story of Africa | Comfort Markwei | TEDxDuke

author: TEDx Talks
description: Speaking from her own experience running for the German Parliament at 19, Anna Ortwein argues that despite Germany normalizing women’s leadership during Angela Merkel’s 2005-2021 chancellorship, women’s representation in the German Bundestag has stagnated at about 32% since 1998, showing that "role-model” leadership alone doesn’t change how candidates are recruited and promoted. Similarly, in the United States, women hold roughly 28% of voting seats in United States Congress. She argues that this underrepresentation points less to an electability problem than to barriers at the point of entry. Using gun violence as an example, she shows how gendered public concerns shape what officials prioritize in office and concludes that increasing women’s political representation — not simply proposing new policies — is what will move stalled issues forward. Anna Ortwein is a sophomore from Germany at Duke University, studying Political Science and Economics. She is passionate about understanding
title: Role models didn’t fix women’s representation in politics. Recruiting will | Anna Ortwein | TEDxDuke

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How often do we answer "How are you?" with "I'm fine" without thinking? For many of us, it's a habit—even when we're overwhelmed, exhausted, or struggling. This talk explores how that simple response contributes to a culture of silence, making it harder to ask for help or recognize when others need support.

Drawing on their work in mental health and community building, the speakers show how choosing honesty over habit can foster deeper connections, empathy, and healing. By reimagining one of our most common daily conversations, the audience is invited to see how saying "I'm not OK" can become the beginning of meaningful dialogue rather than the end of it. Dr. Antija Allen (ann-tee-yuh, al-en) is the Director of the Pellissippi Academic Center for Excellence (PACE) and a tenured Associate Professor of Psychology with over 20 years of experience in higher education. She is the recipient of the Roger Crowe Excellence in Teaching Award and the Staff Excellence Award.

She is the author o
title: The power of saying "I'm not OK" | Dr. Antija Allen & Justin T. Stewart | TEDxFresno State

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TedX Tufts talk, speaker Emily Ruhm explores the complex interaction between vulnerability and humanitarian crises. From her experiences at the UN in New York, with the Peace Corps in Senegal, to foreign aid programming in Lesotho, to writing funding proposals for humanitarian aid in Nigeria, she describes how her definition of vulnerability has changed over time. She has learned to question the systems that are put in place to help people and analyze which people they overlook. She is now pursuing her PhD at Tufts, researching the intersectionality between gender and humanitarian crises. She encourages people to look past ideas of “vulnerable” populations, as this limits one’s agency and discounts other groups who also experience hardships. She emphasizes collecting data on all
parts of a person’s identity - age, race, gender,
disability in order to enhance the “do no harm”
mission of humanitarian aid. She urges us to notice
who is missing in our communities and give a voice
t
title: Beyond victimhood: Reimagining vulnerability in humanitarian crises | Emily Ruhm | TEDxTufts

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In his TEDxTufts talk, speaker Jody Boykins shares his personal interaction with the school-to-prison pipeline in his youth. He shares how his connection to higher education through the Tufts University Prison Initiative opened him up to a vibrant new community, gave him new tools to understand his pain, and transformed education from a space of trauma to a space of belonging. Through this talk,
he hopes to spotlight valuable organizations working to expand opportunities for formerly incarcerated
individuals and highlight the transformative power of
forgiveness, education, and community. Jody Boykins is currently an undergraduate at Tufts
University and have been a student of the TUPIT program
since 2022. His research focuses on adolescents who
struggle with substance abuse, the associated risk and
protective factors, the long-term effects and relation to
incarceration, and the impact of programming on formerly
incarcerated students. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED c
title: How Handcuffs Set Me Free | Jody Boykins | TEDxTufts

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDxTufts talk “The Future is Fiction,” Julie Carrick Dalton illustrates the importance of collaboration between climate fiction writers and scientists. She highlights how science fiction authors such as Jules Verne and E.E. Smith imagined technologies and circumstances that later became reality, demonstrating the power of fiction to anticipate and shape the future. Drawing upon both literary history and her personal experiences with deforestation and forest preservation, Dalton demonstrates how storytelling incites meaningful discourse and action. Climate fiction authors explore not only the environmental, but ethical, political, and emotional repercussions of climate change. Through her talk, Dalton encourages engagement with the climate fiction genre and dialogue between the arts
and sciences to find creative and lasting solutions to the climate crisis. Julie Carrick Dalton is the award-winning author of The Last
Beekeeper, Waiting for the Night Song, and The Forest
Becomes
title: The Future is Fiction | Julie Dalton | TEDxTufts

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDxTufts talk, Seona Maskara explores a powerful idea: young people cannot meaningfully shape democracy if their basic needs and sense of belonging are unmet. Drawing on her research at the Center for Information and Research on Civic Learning and Engagement (CIRCLE) at Tufts University, as well as her own lived experience, she introduces the concept of a “political home”, a space where young people can belong, develop their political identities, meet their basic needs, and build the confidence to lead. Through research findings, personal stories, and practical examples, Seona argues that civic engagement is not just about voting or activism, but about community. At a time when 85% of youth lack access to supportive civic spaces, she challenges organizations — and all of us — to help build the political homes young people need to feel seen, heard, and empowered. Seona Maskara (A26) has served as a research assistant at
the Center for Information and Research on Civic Learning
title: ‘Political homes’ for youth: Supporting belonging and civic engagement | Seona Maskara | TEDxTufts

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In his TEDxTufts Talk, John O’Brien explores the hidden impact of everyday incivility starting with a personal experience of rudeness. He talks about his professional journey dealing with incivil colleagues and environments that made him doubt his ability as a professor. Not only does incivility impact people on a personal level, but it also hurts companies, monetarily and society as a whole which John explores through various statistics described in Christiane Porath’s book He introduces a simple and actionable framework: BAM (Breathing, Active Listening, Mindfulness) offering practical tools to interrupt the cycle. In a culture where everyday rudeness feels increasingly normalized, John challenges us to choose civility and become everyday superheroes in our interactions. John M. O'Brien, Ph.D. is a clinical psychologist, author, and
expert in civility and interpersonal communication. Dr.
O'Brien is dedicated to promoting kindness, mutual respect,
and healthier relationships in both
title: Small Slights, Big Consequences: The Power of Everyday Incivility | John O'Brien | TEDxTufts

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Audrey Appleby and Deborah Schwartz graduated from Tufts University more than 50 years ago. The two women will reflect on their unique paths – Deborah on her career as a healthcare lawyer, and
her journey to the peak of the highest mountain in Africa, and Audrey, her career as a creative artist, merging her passion for dance and music with her fascination with psychology. Both women share how they reinvented themselves in the face of unexpected challenges and unimaginable loss, inspiring a new generation of Tufts students to apply their skills and passions and get creative in the face of adversity. Audrey Appleby studied Psychology and Drama at Tufts,
Dance MFA Studies at Sarah Lawrence, and MBA at NYU
Stern Graduate School of Business. Embracing her
entrepreneurial spirit, she launched the career passion of her
life, creating MagicDance On The Water, a Dance and Music
School with Dance and Dance Therapy for ages one to 100.
She is also a Singer Songwriter.

Deborah is a Tufts graduat
title: When the Ground Breaks, Be Groundbreaking | Audrey Appleby & Deborah Schwartz | TEDxTufts

author: TEDx Talks
description:
He explores why so many capable, driven people, at every level, feel stuck despite their success and what it actually takes to move forward. Rather than focusing on what people do or how they do it, this talk examines the internal shifts that unlock forward momentum. Through his MVP concept, speech shows how aligning mindset, vision, and purpose helps people stop settling; reconnect with what matters; and step into the next version of themselves, one intentional choice at a time.
 Brian Alementi is an acclaimed Inspirational Keynote Speaker, award-winning leader, certified Master Trainer and CEO of Alementi Elevates, LLC. He is renowned for engaging presentations that combine inspiration with practical, actionable insights. With a rich background in guiding and elevating teams, Brian brings his experience as a previous leader within a Fortune 500 company’s Hall of Fame learning and development division, where his dedication to growth and excellence shaped high-performing teams across
title: You Didn’t Come This Far to Stop Now | Brian Alementi | TEDxSST Corpus Christi Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Human identity isn’t a solo performance — it’s a symphony played by trillions of microbial partners. Chandrima Bhattacharya, Cornell University PhD candidate, takes us on a journey to some of the planet's most extreme environments and introduces us to the residents: microbes.  Chandrima Bhattacharya is a computational biologist and PhD candidate at Weill Cornell Medicine who explores the surprising ways microbes adapt to the harshest places on—and off—our planet. Working in the labs of Dr. Christopher Mason and Dr. Jan Krumsiek, she studies microbial life in radiological sites, deep‑sea lakes, urban superfund zones, and even aboard the International Space Station. Using metagenomics, machine learning, and genome mining, she uncovers the hidden strategies microbes use to survive and the clues they offer for new medicines. Chandrima has contributed to landmark spaceflight and global microbiome studies, with work published in Nature, Cell, and Nature Microbiology. She is passionate about
title: Microbes, our invisible superheroes | Chandrima Bhattacharya | TEDxRiverdale

author: TEDx Talks
description: All paths face roadblocks at some point; Samhita faced hers when she reached a turning point in her gymnastics career last year and discovered the true value of second chances. Samhita Narayanan loves music and the arts and has pursued competitive gymnastics for twelve years. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Ability To Try Again | Samhita Narayanan | TEDxFCSIA Youth

Viraj Das has a passion for coding, public speaking, and creating once-in-a-lifetime experiences. He spends much of his time working in AI and VR, and much of that work has been recognized through awards and competitive achievement. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Through Other Eyes | Viraj Das | TEDxFCSIA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In our endless pursuit of digital innovation, businesses have embraced kiosks, AI bots, and automated interfaces at the expense of true hospitality and human connection. Angela Webber argues that a digital interface can't smile, understand frustration, or build a relationship—leaving both customers and employees feeling unseen and transactional. Citing alarming stats on toxic leadership and customer retention, Webber calls on organizations to realize that their frontline is their bottom line. Drawing inspiration from George Bernard Shaw's "A Splendid Torch," she delivers a powerful plea to choose people over automated efficiency and restore human connection to customer service. Angela Webber has spent over three decades working in customer service and organizational culture. She advocates for returning authentic human compassion and empathy to customer experience and leadership, warning against replacing genuine connection with digital efficiency. This talk was given at a TEDx event u
title: The Splendid Torch | Angela Webber | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: In the United States, someone suffers a stroke every 40 seconds—a reality Trevor Shoemaker experienced firsthand after surviving both a hemorrhagic and an ischemic stroke. Waking up to hemiparesis, memory loss, and a life restricted to a wheelchair, Trevor faced a crucial choice: succumb to anger or embrace a mindset of recovery and faith. Detailing his grueling daily journey through physical, occupational, and speech therapy, Shoemaker demonstrates how choosing kindness, maintaining a positive attitude, and relying on community can open doors that anger would keep locked. Trevor Shoemaker is an app developer, sports handicapper, and stroke survivor. After surviving a life-threatening stroke, Trevor uses his platform to share honest insights into neurological rehabilitation, memory recovery, and the transformative power of mindset and community support. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at h
title: Every 40 Seconds | Trevor Shoemaker | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: As a single father, Carl Cleavenger dedicated his life to pushing past the limits of his special-needs son, James, building his physical strength and speech through beach walks, ocean swimming, jet skiing, and dune buggying. But when a tragic fuel-line explosion took James's life and left Carl with third-degree burns over 50% of his body, Carl was forced to face an agonizing physical and emotional recovery. Driven by music, ocean movement, and a former boxer's wisdom—that "it's not how many times you go down, it's how many times you get up"—Cleavenger delivers a moving story on resilience, grief, and refusing to give up before the final bell rings. Carl Cleavenger is a father, advocate, and burn survivor. In his talk "The Bell Hasn't Rung," Carl shares his story of raising his special-needs son James through movement and outdoor adventures, followed by surviving a catastrophic fire that left over half of his body with third-degree burns. Through six weeks of intensive care, seven surg
title: The Bell Hasn't Rung | Carl Clavenger | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Paa Kwesi Folson challenges one of Africa’s most popular pieces of advice: “If you can’t get a job, start a business.” He argues that while entrepreneurship is often celebrated as Africa’s path to transformation, too much of it is driven by circumstance rather than intention. 

Drawing a distinction between circumstantial and intentional entrepreneurs, Paa Kwesi Folson explores why businesses born purely from survival rarely create large-scale impact. 

Through powerful stories, practical insights, and his Intentional Entrepreneur Framework, he presents a compelling case for raising a generation of entrepreneurs who build not just to survive, but to transform Africa.  Paa Kwesi Folson is an award-winning public speaker, entrepreneur, and thought leadership strategist from Ghana. Known as the “Certified Gem Provider,” he is recognized for his insights in communication, thought leadership, personal and business growth.

He is the founder of Revolead
title: The Silent Problem of Entrepreneurship in Africa | Paa Kwesi Folson | TEDxUniversityofCapeCoast

author: TEDx Talks
description: Two hundred and fifty years ago, ordinary people with the right tools rewrote the future. Today, artificial intelligence—specifically "Agentic AI" acting as a digital peer—presents the same transformative potential. Drawing on real-world examples of an overworked 7th-grade teacher, a supply chain strategist, and a family farm in Kansas, Andy Bhattacharya demonstrates how AI isn't here to take human jobs; it is here to remove drowning paperwork, optimize decisions, and restore human capacity. Bhattacharya delivers a compelling call to democratize AI tools so that educators, small businesses, and farmers alike have equal access to the future. Andy Bhattacharya is an innovation and technology strategist who explores the intersection of emerging technologies and human adaptability. His work focuses on guiding organizations and individuals through digital transformations while emphasizing human-centric problem solving. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: The New Declaration | Andy Bhattacharya | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: This OSHA Compliance Officer, and former officer in the US Army Chemical Corps speaks of her experience as an immigrant, a military officer, and a leader, and how living a life filled with boundaries and breaking them down has led to her success and happiness. Olja Correa is a Compliance Assistance Specialist with OSHA’s Tampa Area Office, where she leads outreach, alliance initiatives, and strategic partnerships. With a background as a Compliance Safety and Health Officer and industrial hygienist, Olja has spent over a decade working at the intersection of public safety, health, and education. Prior to OSHA, she served as a commissioned officer in the United States Army Chemical Corps, holding multiple leadership roles in special operations. Her experience reflects a deep commitment to safety, leadership, and service. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Boundaries: What are they to you? | Olja Correa | TEDxYouth@PHUHS

author: TEDx Talks
description: When children enter kindergarten, educators meticulously design an environment where they feel safe, supported, and cared for—yet as adults, we often shift our focus solely to tasks and outputs, neglecting the culture we live in. Extending Rita Pierson's famous insight that "every child deserves a champion," educator and Villanova professor Scott Weinstein argues that every adult deserves a champion, too. Drawing on lessons from impactful mentors and his experience leading schools, Weinstein demonstrates that if you are not intentional about the culture you wish to create, one will form without you—and it may not be the one you want. Scott Weinstein is a longtime educator, former principal across elementary, middle, and high school levels, and faculty member at Villanova University. In his talk "Culture by Design," he shares how intentionally designing supportive environments around people fosters lifelong belonging and human thriving. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED
title: Culture by design | Scott Weinstein | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: Our boundaries are shaped by culture, family, and the experiences that define us; and sometimes, they need to be redrawn. Growing up in Trinidad taught this speaker the power of community, shared responsibility, and belonging, while immigrating to America introduced boundaries built around privacy, independence, and individual achievement. Through motherhood, career challenges, and the loss of her traditional village support system, she discovered that some boundaries protect us, while others can isolate us. Her message is not to tear boundaries down, but to redraw them with intention to protect what matters while making room for connection, community, and the people who help us thrive. Heidi Dindial-Thompson is a social studies teacher at Palm Harbor University High School, where she is dedicated to helping students understand the world through history, civic engagement, and critical thinking. With years of experience in education, she brings a thoughtful, real-world perspective to d
title: Redrawing the Lines That Raised Us | Heidi Dindial Thompson | TEDxYouth@PHUHS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Being the first is an achievement. Making sure you're not the last is a legacy. Offaih shares a powerful reflection on courage, representation, and the responsibility that comes with opening new doors. True leadership isn't measured by personal milestones but by the opportunities we create for others. In the spirit of KEDU, this talk reminds us that our greatest impact is often found in the lives we make easier to rise.  Iyom A. J. Offiah (Chief Mrs. Anayo Justina Offiah), SAN is a distinguished Nigerian lawyer and legal reform advocate from Enugu State. She studied Law at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 1978.
In 2003, she made history as the first female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) from the old Eastern Region. She also served as Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Enugu State and became the first female Chairman of the Nigerian Bar Association, Enugu Branch.
Iyom Offiah is widely respected for her contributions to justice refo
title: The Real Work Begins After the Breakthrough  | IYOM, A. J. Offiah | TEDxNzaStreet

author: TEDx Talks
description: As a professional wedding MC and entertainer, Matt Music spent years relying on a sharp tongue and humor to survive on stage—and in life. But after a series of painful missteps, including a $2 million mistake born from refusing to read the room, he realized that true communication isn't about performing or pushing through; it's about awareness. Sharing his core framework of Energy, Engagement, and Alignment, Music breaks down how self-consciousness and screen-driven disconnection blind us to the people in front of us. He challenges us to move from "Always Be Closing" to "Always Be Connecting"—proving that real human connection requires us to get out of our heads and actually care. Matt Music is a speaker and communication expert focused on interpersonal connection. Through his E/E/A framework (Emotion, Engagement, Alignment), Matt helps leaders and speakers close the gap between what they intend to communicate and what their audience actually perceives. This talk was given at a TEDx e
title: What we often get wrong about communication | Matt Music | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: We all face “icebergs” every day, but why do we so often look the other way? From the Titanic to suffering around us today, this talk explores why we minimize other people’s pain, ignore warning signs, and convince ourselves that someone else will step in. Most importantly, it reveals how we can recognize the icebergs around us and choose to keep each other afloat. Anvitha Barun is a high school student, speaker, and entrepreneur passionate about understanding human behavior and creating meaningful social impact. Through research, storytelling, and community projects, she explores how psychology shapes the choices we make and how small individual actions can lead to lasting change. In her TED talk, she examines what the story of the Titanic reveals about human nature and why choosing to act, rather than look away, matters more than ever. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.c
title: Why We Ignore Icebergs: The Cost of Looking Away | Anvitha Barun | TEDxBallantyne Ridge Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Standing half-naked and barefoot in the snow while watching his house burn down, Obet Pabon realized his dreams weren't being destroyed—they were being fireproofed. Drawing on his experiences with personal loss and business setbacks, Pabon introduces the "WOW Mindset": Withstand the storm, Own your story, and Win by rising from the ashes. He demonstrates how our greatest scars transform us into seeds, inspiring others through our resilience and proving that even when we feel buried, we are actually being planted. Obet Pabon is a transformational speaker and leadership mentor. His talks focus on helping individuals overcome personal adversity, identify core purpose, and unlock full potential in both personal life and team environments. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The New Declaration | Obet Pabon | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: A single question asked to a Fortune 100 executive during a doctoral research interview—"What do you dream about?"—unlocked an unexpected, transformative human connection. Dr. Dan Docherty explores how intentional curiosity can solve our modern relational crisis in a world dominated by phone distractions and hyper-task focus. Backed by neuroscience, Docherty introduces the concept of the "Dream Leader"—a philosophy and practice that activates our parasympathetic nervous system, builds deep trust through oxytocin, and helps us truly see and interpret the dreams of those around us. Dr. Dan Docherty is Chief Coaching Officer at Braintrust and a Professor of Leadership at Miami University. His talk, "What Do You Dream About?", focuses on how a single transformational question can shift nervous systems from protective fear to aspirational connection, creating authentic engagement and relational connection in leadership. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format bu
title: What Do You Dream About? | Dr. Dan Docherty | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: After losing his mother at age 13, professional triathlete Matt Russell learned to channel grief into relentless endurance sports. But at the 2017 Ironman World Championship, while moving at 35 mph, he collided head-first with a vehicle, severing his jugular vein and nearly bleeding to death. Refusing to let trauma end his career, Russell rebuilt his life through three core practices: daily gratitude journaling, breathwork, and building confidence through intentional action. Just one year after his catastrophic accident, he returned to Hawaii to place 6th in the world, demonstrating how intentional gratitude can become the ultimate competitive advantage in overcoming adversity. Matt Russell is a top professional Ironman triathlete with over 40 podium finishes. After losing his mother at age 13 and surviving a near-fatal bike crash at the Kona Ironman World Championship that severed his jugular vein, he shares how radical gratitude became his ultimate competitive advantage and life phi
title: Gratitude Wins | Matt Russell | TEDxSoards Road

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the chaos you've been trying to escape is actually trying to tell you something? Inspired by the idea of Laavanyadhooram, a Malayalam word describing the unique distance from which something appears most beautiful. Mridul George takes us on an exploration of perspective and purpose, sharing how embracing multiple identities led to the three realisations that made chaos his direction. Born and raised in Muvattupuzha, Kerala, Mridul George followed a path familiar to many, an engineering education, followed by over a decade in the IT industry. Yet alongside spreadsheets, code, and corporate deadlines, another life was taking shape. From school and college days onward, he was a storyteller, writing, anchoring television programs, and learning early what it meant to speak to an audience. This duality would later define his work: creativity tempered by discipline, emotion structured by intent. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently org
title: Finding Laavanyadhooram: How Chaos Became My Compass | Mridul George | TEDxTIST
